title: Tools, extracted (fhir-harness)
description: Candidate terms extracted from every Tool node: `title` as the label, `description` as the definition, the Tool id as the code. Generated by folio-assistant-core/scripts/glossary-extract.ts; not curated, and never hand-edited: a person promotes a term by authoring it in a glossary of their own.

terms.prefLabel: Stage one IG as its own just-the-docs Jekyll site
terms.definition: Turn an IG source repository into ONE Jekyll source for just-the-docs, as the IG Publisher builds one IG per site: `input/pagecontent` pages with title, parent and order from `sushi-config.yaml` `pages:`, the files the Publisher's include tags resolve against, images, `_data/fhir.json` from `ig-site-data`, and a `_config.yml`. The pages render unchanged, including their references to the IG's site data (bean `bamf`, owner's choice of one site per IG). With the IG's menu, the layout is the one every IG site wears (bean `mftp`): the IG's own top bar, the IG's TOC declared as the folio-assistant navbar's section (added by `rail-standalone-pages`), no sidebar of its own, an edit link per page, and per heading a source-line link and a pre-filled feedback issue.

terms.prefLabel: Check a Questionnaire field for field against the wireframe it was derived from
terms.definition: Compare the `data-element` fields of a mid-fidelity wireframe (per `data-layout`, in document order) with the answerable items of a BUILT Questionnaire (depth first, named by `definition` or `code`). Reports a field with no item, an item with no field, an item naming no data element, a data element twice in one layout, and the first place the order differs. Fidelity, not design. Moved down from the WHO layer on the owner's ruling of 2026-10-14: nothing in it is WHO's.

terms.prefLabel: Seed the FHIR package cache from trusted sources (exact versions)
terms.definition: Fill `~/.fhir/packages` (or `--cache`) for an environment that cannot reach packages.fhir.org, from trust anchors only: npm account `grahamegrieve` (owner-trusted), publishers' own published-site repositories (the seeder's list, each fetch verified against the tarball's own package.json), template repos found through FHIR/ig-registry's templates.json read live each run, and an owner `--mirror`. Exact versions only (a patch wildcard resolves as the Publisher resolves it, recorded); every tarball verified; nothing computed once and kept; provenance recorded; missing versions listed, never substituted.

terms.prefLabel: Mirror FHIR packages from packages.fhir.org into a git repository
terms.definition: On a machine that reaches packages.fhir.org, fetch exactly a missing list (from `fhir-cache-seed-npm --missing-out`), check each tarball names itself exactly, record SHA512SUMS, and commit and push to a git repository that an environment without packages.fhir.org reads with `--mirror`. The person running it is the trust anchor for what it adds.

terms.prefLabel: FSH dependency cone
terms.definition: Compute the dependency cone over an IG's FSH graph, and the blast radius of a set of changed files. What makes an incremental IG build possible: without it, any edit rebuilds everything.

terms.prefLabel: Write one JSON-LD node per IG artefact, and check a built site's nodes
terms.definition: `write` turns an artefact index into `artifact/<Type>-<id>.jsonld` (and a `.json` twin) under a docs root: one `folio-ig-artifact-jsonld/v1` node per artefact, in borrowed vocabularies only (the FHIR RDF class, dcterms, schema.org, PROV), naming the artefact's canonical URL, its representations and, for a compiled copy, what built it. `check` is the kind's QA: over a BUILT site, every artefact has its node and no node is an orphan, each node is its own file's, its twin matches, and every local resource it names is on the site. It also writes and checks the index node, `artifact/index.jsonld` (`folio-ig-artifact-index-jsonld/v1`): every artefact once, each entry naming its node. WHO-free; the assets the thin pages render (owner, 2026-10-11, option A; thin by default since 2026-10-12).

terms.prefLabel: List and view the delta between two IG ASTs
terms.definition: Diff two ASTs by resource key: added, removed, changed (with a structural element-level differential) and version-changed resources, plus edges added and removed; optionally fold in the incremental plan, and render just-the-docs pages (an index that lists, a page per resource that shows) every one of which carries the provisional mark. `list <ast>` summarises one AST.

terms.prefLabel: Build an IG and write its AST
terms.definition: Run one ordinary IG Publisher build through `AstPublisher` (a subclass that overrides nothing) and write the AST beside `output/`: one JSON file per resource keyed `canonical|version`, `dependencies.json` (upstream's DependencyAnalyser plus the Library/PlanDefinition/ActivityDefinition/Measure edges it leaves empty), SUSHI's `fsh-index.json`, and a manifest that declares itself a cache and records the inputs it is valid for.

terms.prefLabel: Rebuild only the cone of a change and merge it into the AST
terms.definition: Write the unchanged part of a base AST as a FHIR package into the package cache, build a temporary IG of only the rebuild set with the stock Publisher, merge the result into a mixed-provenance AST (`builtAt` per resource), and repeat while the merged graph's cone reaches resources that were not rebuilt.

terms.prefLabel: Export an IG AST as JSON-LD
terms.definition: Write an AST as linked data against `fhir-harness/schemas/ig-ast.context.jsonld`: each resource a node identified by its canonical URL (`urn:fhir:<Type>/<id>` when it has none) and typed by its FHIR resource type, each dependency edge a link to its target, and the manifest's `authority: cache` and `provisional` list carried on the graph. The AST is validated against the Zod declaration the JSON Schemas are generated from before it is exported (bean `l0lq`).

terms.prefLabel: Summarise one IG AST
terms.definition: Counts per resource type, edges in total and resolved inside the IG, edges by origin (upstream's DependencyAnalyser or ast-export's LogicEdges), whether the AST is mixed-provenance and how many resources each revision built, and what the manifest declares provisional.

terms.prefLabel: Measure the AST export on real IGs
terms.definition: Build the WHO SMART Trust and Immunizations IGs through `ig-ast-export` and print the W1/W2 measurements: counts, whether FSH sources sit where the plan expects, and logic-layer edge coverage per resource type against 458 of 458. `--byte-identical` adds a stock build and an `output/` diff.

terms.prefLabel: Write the IG AST viewer: a page per instance holding `ig-ast` directories, and a hub
terms.definition: For every visualiser an instance declares `renderedBy: ig-ast-pages`, write the hub at `<locale>/<harness>/<id>/` and, with `subgraphs: "instance"`, one page per instance that declares an `ig-ast` directory, at `…/<instance>/`. Each lists the ASTs the directory holds: the IG's package id, resources in total and by type, dependency edges (resolved inside the IG, by origin, by kind), the rebuild plan when one is recorded, and what stays provisional. A declared directory not on disk — a branch-family member not restored, which is the normal case — is reported UNKNOWN with the family it would be restored from, never as zero ASTs. Not `ig-ast-list` extended: that Tool summarises ONE AST it is handed, and a site build has no AST path to hand it.

terms.prefLabel: Plan an incremental IG build from a delta of changed files
terms.definition: Map a delta (a commit range, a PR's diff, or the staged index) onto a base AST: which resources to rebuild (the forward cone), which to load from cache, which to remove, or a full build and why. Builds nothing.

terms.prefLabel: Refresh an IG's AST cache on a runner
terms.definition: Dispatch an IG repository's `ig-ast-refresh.yml`, which calls fhir-harness's reusable `.github/workflows/ig-ast-refresh.yml`: mount the layers the IG's index.lock.json pins, restore and judge the cache for `ref`, and when it is not valid (or `force`) run the caller's optional `pre-export` overlay command and build the IG with the pinned Publisher AST exporter (the AST is recorded against the clean commit's inputs, the overlay's changes put back), check the new AST is valid for its commit, and seed `cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id>` with `ig-cache seed --push` — only from a commit on the default branch with the tip's inputs. Builds no site, writes no gh-pages, dispatches nothing.

terms.prefLabel: Render a computed IG AST delta as just-the-docs pages
terms.definition: Write the pages for a delta already computed by `ig-ast-diff --json`: an index that lists, a page per changed resource that shows, every one opening with the provisional mark and with Liquid in values neutralised.

terms.prefLabel: Is this IG AST still valid for the IG's current inputs?
terms.definition: Run folio-assistant-core's `compiledValidity` on an AST manifest's `inputs`: recompute the input digest (the same algorithm as the Java writer, pinned by a shared golden vector) and the source revision, and answer valid, stale-inputs (naming which input), or cannot-tell.

terms.prefLabel: Measure the IG Publisher's binary outputs on a pages branch
terms.definition: Read a pages branch's git tree and report the Publisher's binary outputs (full-ig.zip, package.tgz and variants, package.db, validator packs, the definitions/examples/expansions zips, spreadsheets) by name: copies, bytes, and how much of it sits in branch previews. Reads the tree, never a checkout, so a multi-gigabyte branch costs a depth-1 fetch.

terms.prefLabel: FHIR AST cache
terms.definition: Restore, verify, seed and diagnose the prebuilt AST artefacts for an IG. Always try `restore` first: a full AST build via AstExportCli is expensive, a restore is fast.

terms.prefLabel: Generate an IG instance's reader-facing pages from its artefact index
terms.definition: Write `<instance>/docs/` — an index page, one page per artefact, a page per over-large category and per menu group — from `fhir-artifact-index/index.json` (and `menu.json` when ingested), styled by the template chrome an owning instance ingested. Moved down to this layer because nothing in it was one IG's own (#1767); with `--summary` it writes an instance's landing page, opening with that instance's harness section. For an instance whose docs declare `igSite` (bean `mftp`) it writes no index, menu or category pages — the IG site's own replace them — and only a front-matter `artifacts.md` naming the Tool that drew it. Where an instance declares a visualiser `renderedBy: ig-pages`, it also writes that visualiser's route page, `<base>/<instance>/<id>/`, which opens the artefact index; with `--site <dir>` it writes only those route pages, under that site. For an IG whose SOURCE is at hand, `build-ig-site` renders the IG's own pages instead; this is for an IG known only by what it published.

terms.prefLabel: Build an IG repository's own site from its cached AST, with no instance declaration
terms.definition: The three checkout scripts the platform's site build runs for a repository that holds an IG and only mounts layers (`index.config.json`): `ig-site:ast` restores the AST from the IG's cache branch (`ig-cache.sh restore`) and judges it, refusing a stale, cannot-tell or absent one (a stale one is accepted for a preview with `SITE_ACCEPT_STALE_AST=1`); `ig-site:compose` derives the artefact index from the AST (binding any IG API sidecars a layer above left in `$SITE_WORK/ig-api/`), writes the thin artefact pages, stages the IG's `input/` and `sushi-config.yaml` (menu read at build time, palette from the webpage theme of the top layer the repository mounts, edit links from its origin) and composes it at the ROOT of the host site source; `ig-site:publisher-pages` serves the AST's resources (`ast-data/` and `<Type>-<id>.json`), the artefact index and the sidecars, refuses a page wearing the IG Publisher's chrome, repairs repeated element ids and stamps `folio-build.json`. Never runs the Publisher and never reads its output. Compose lists the pages it puts in the site in `FOLIO_SITE_UPSTREAM_PAGES`, so the site build reports the IG's own dead links rather than refusing the publish over them.

terms.prefLabel: Populate site.data.fhir for a just-the-docs IG render
terms.definition: Write the IG Publisher's Jekyll variables (`site.data.fhir.ig.*`, `packageId`, `canonical`) for ONE implementation guide, from `sushi-config.yaml` or a published IG's `fhir-artifact-index`, so pages written for the Publisher render on just-the-docs unchanged. fhir-harness declares `site.data` as a pass-through Liquid prefix; this is what Jekyll then reads (bean `bamf`).

terms.prefLabel: Ingest an IG's navigation from its sushi-config
terms.definition: Read `menu:` (and the page tree) out of an IG source repository's `sushi-config.yaml` into `fhir-artifact-index/menu.json`, recording the repository and commit it was read at — the declared source `stage-ig-sites` clones. `--check` re-derives it against a checkout; with no `--source` it reports COULD NOT DETERMINE and exits 2, never 0.

terms.prefLabel: Record an IG's GitHub releases as pointers to their binary assets
terms.definition: Read an IG repository's GitHub releases and write `fhir-artifact-index/releases.json` (`ig-releases/v1`): each asset's name, size, SHA-256 digest and download URL, never its bytes. The IG site's generated `releases` page lists them (bean `b8ip`).

terms.prefLabel: ValueSet expansions → JSON-LD
terms.definition: JSON-LD vocabularies built from the ValueSet expansions in the published output.

terms.prefLabel: Logical models → JSON Schema
terms.definition: A JSON Schema per logical model, from the published FHIR resources.

terms.prefLabel: Snapshot a published IG's terminology at its pinned version
terms.definition: Read every CodeSystem concept out of a FHIR IG clone checked out at its pinned tag and write a `folio-pinned-terminology/v1` snapshot: the offline, version-fixed answer `check:term-mapping` resolves its `fhir` target against. Which IG, which pin record and which snapshot path are the caller's (`--pin`, `--out`, `--source`); this layer names none (#1767, stage B′).

terms.prefLabel: Check an IG's built Questionnaires with CSIRO's SDC libraries
terms.definition: Build-time Structured Data Capture checks, one result per Questionnaire (`sdcChecks[]` of `fhir-questionnaire-wireframe`): `assemble` (`@aehrc/sdc-assemble` 2.0.3: an assemble-root's sub-forms resolve in this IG, and `--out` writes the assembled Questionnaire), `template-extract` (`@aehrc/sdc-template-extract` 1.0.16: extraction from the IG's fixture response yields the expected resources), `populate` (`@aehrc/sdc-populate` 4.7.2: FHIRPath pre-population from a fixture context gives the expected answers) and `behaviour` (`@aehrc/questionnaire-test-toolkit` 0.1.0: the IG's own behavioural test, warn-only). Owner, 2026-10-14: checks, not UI.

terms.prefLabel: Stage every IG whose instance records its source, one Jekyll site each
terms.definition: For every instance holding `fhir-artifact-index/menu.json` with a sushi-config source, clone the IG at the recorded commit and stage it with `build-ig-site`: the instance's webpage theme (inherited along `needs` when it declares none), its artefact pages and `artifacts` page, its post-processing fills, and an edit link to the IG's default branch. An instance whose docs directory declares `igSite` is staged to be served AT `/<instance>/` with its artefact pages copied in (a collision is refused); otherwise beside it at `/<instance>/ig/`. Prints one `<instance> <jekyll source> <at>` line per IG for the caller's `jekyll build` (beans `bamf`, `mftp`).

terms.prefLabel: Strip binary payloads from Library resources
terms.definition: Remove base64 `content.data` from published `Library` resources, so an IG embedding compiled CQL does not ship the bytes twice.

terms.prefLabel: Replace inline Library content with URL references
terms.definition: Replace inline CQL/ELM in `Library` resources with a URL reference to the published copy.

terms.prefLabel: Write an IG site's static terminology index from the IG's own cache
terms.definition: Read the IG Publisher's `expansions.json` and `txcache/`, as `ig-cache.sh restore` leaves them, and write `index.json` (gzipped as `index.json.gz` over 1 MB): every code with its system and display, and each value set's codes. The IG site's service worker answers the self-hosted Form Builder's LOINC search from it, and its UCUM search from the vendored full UCUM list, so the site makes no cross-site call (owner, 2026-10-14: "cache + ucum. this is gh-pages so no XSS"). `build-ig-site` runs it for every IG with a Questionnaire.

terms.prefLabel: ValueSets → JSON Schema
terms.definition: A JSON Schema per ValueSet, plus the enumeration-response schemas published at the IG root.
